title: trajectory-commitments-lightboard-and-all-team-qna-script-v0-1
content:
Purpose
This is a working facilitator pack for the next company-wide sync (90-day trajectory check). It bundles the proposed company OKR slate, an executive readout crib, and a short, adaptable lightboard script + all-team Q&A runbook. The goal: give execs concise talking points, give hosts simple visual cues, and make the Q&A feel owned and low-friction.

Background (quick context)
- We are in the third month of the current quarter; usage and cost telemetry show mixed signals across Hosted API and Dedicated segments.
- Product roadmaps have a handful of cross-team dependencies (Dedicated autoscale policy changes, Private deployment KMS integration, Optimize rollout experiments) that need alignment now to avoid end-of-quarter scramble.
- This doc is intentionally light: meant to be a single-sheet prep + a short on-stage script for the senior presenters, not a replaceable long-form strategy doc.

Scope of this doc
- Proposed company-level OKRs for the 90-day arc (draft).
- Executive readout: 3-minute CEO script + 2-minute VP Eng addendum + 90-second Ops highlight.
- Lightboard visuals and stage cues (what to show on screen during each 90–120s block).
- Q&A triage protocol and a prioritized question list to seed conversation.

Proposed 90‑day Company OKRs (draft)
Objective A: Make inference predictable at scale (latency & cost)
  KR A1: Reduce 95th percentile tail latency for hosted text-generate by 20% vs baseline (baseline = 2026-01-01–2026-01-31).
  KR A2: Decrease per‑million‑token unit cost on median production workload by 12% using batching + quantization configs recommended by Optimize.
  KR A3: Achieve successful fallback-to-variant routing in 99.5% of simulated capacity-loss exercises (automated test).

Objective B: Increase enterprise adoption for Dedicated & Private
  KR B1: Close 4 Dedicated pilot contracts (>= $100k ARR each) with SLA and capacity commitments defined.
  KR B2: Deliver Private on-prem installer + KMS integration for first regulated customer; on‑board in <= 6 weeks.
  KR B3: Reduce time-to-onboard for Dedicated from contract signature to production by 35%.

Objective C: Developer velocity and QA for model rollouts
  KR C1: Ship rollout automation (canary + automatic rollback on quality regression) for any model in the catalog; 90% of new model rollouts to use the flow.
  KR C2: Expand evals coverage: add 10 representative prompt sets across top 5 vertical customers and enable continuous monitoring.
  KR C3: Reduce regression mean-time-to-detect from customer reports to alerting by 40%.

Notes on these OKRs
- These are company-level; each product and functional group should derive 1–3 supporting OKRs.
- We intentionally limited the count to keep the all-hands message focused.

Executive readout (speaker crib)
CEO (3 minutes):
  - Opening framing (30s): "Last quarter we prioritized production economics and predictable SLAs. Today we’re sharing where that investment is paying off and where we still need focus."
  - Wins (60s): rapid bullets: Dedicated pilots traction, Optimize algorithm showing early cost wins on test workloads, reliability story where automatic fallback prevented a customer outage during a region disruption. Call out customer names only with permission.
  - Known gaps (45s): tail-latency hotspots, onboarding friction for Private, and an ask to engineering and customer success to converge on the top two blockers for immediate sprint focus.
  - Close with clarity (45s): announce the three company OKRs for the quarter and the single prioritization ask: "One prioritized backlog item per team that moves an OKR needle."

VP Eng (2 minutes):
  - Technical snapshot: two slides: (1) latency distribution before/after recent kernel changes; (2) pipeline for rollout automation and how teams can opt in.
  - Short action: owners for fallback and batching changes (names + 30/60 day checkpoints).

VP Product Ops / SRE (90 seconds):
  - Operational focus: how the Console dashboards will expose token-level cost breakdowns and regression alerts.
  - Ask CS: highlight two pilot customers for dedicated support.

Lightboard visuals & on-stage cues (one-line directions to the A/V team)
- Slide 0 (30s pre-roll): calm background, agenda bullets (2 lines).
- Slide 1 (CEO wins): three icons (Dedicated, Optimize, Reliability) with one-sentence captions. Hold for 60s.
- Slide 2 (OKR visual): single chord diagram showing Objective -> top KR bullets. Presenter points to each objective in sequence.
- Slide 3 (Q&A prompt): "Questions? Use mic or Slack #company-questions" with triage lanes visible: Product | Engineering | Sales | Other.

All-team Q&A runbook (how we handle questions live)
- Triage roles: Moderator (assignable), Subject matter buffers (eng/product ops, cs), Notetaker (Document owner).
- Micro-protocol: questions written in Slack or using mic. If the question is tactical (Jiraable), note and commit to a follow-up in 48 hours. If strategic/policy-level, escalate to exec inbox and schedule a 30-minute follow-up within 2 weeks.
- Rapid-scan script for Moderator: repeat the question (10–15s), name the buffer, offer a 60s answer; if longer, defer to follow-up.

Seeded FAQ (likely questions and one-sentence answers to help moderators)
Q: How will this affect token pricing for startups?
A: No immediate pricing change; optimization efforts aim to lower costs for all tiers over the quarter and we'll communicate any pricing adjustments 30 days in advance.

Q: What happens if a Dedicated customer needs out-of-band capacity?
A: We have a burst-capacity policy draft — CS + sales will finalize contract addendum templates this week and publish to the Docs site.

Q: When can teams expect the rollout automation?
A: First internal rollout flows will be available in beta next month; we will collect internal feedback before a controlled public rollout.

Logistics & timeline
- Pre-read (send 48 hours before): this doc + one-page OKR one-pager.
- Rehearsal (mandatory for speakers): 2 days before event; 20–30 minute slot with A/V and moderators.
- All-hands date: TBD (propose 2026-03-18 afternoon PT).
- Follow-up: publish recording + decisions doc within 48 hours, and create a tracking board for OKR supporters (owner + 30/60-day checkpoints).

Action items (quick owners)
- Riley Morgan: finalize Dedicated pilot slide + 1-pager by 2026-03-03.
- Samir Desai: confirm fallback test metrics and prepare scripted demo (2026-03-07).
- Noelle Park: create the pre-read one-pager and Slack thread (2026-03-10).
- Avery Chen (owner): shepherd final facilitator script and produce the triage doc (2026-03-12).

Risks and open questions (notes to self)
- Risk: too many cross-cutting asks in the all-hands will dilute focus; mitigant: pick one operational ask per team.
- Open: do we permit customer mentions during wins? (Legal/PR guidance needed).
- Open: will the Console retention tier support the planned analytics demo? (Confirm storage + retention costs).

Appendix: rehearsal micro-script (for the CEO)
[Start] "Hi — quick frame: last quarter we doubled down on performance and predictability. Today we will share where that investment is paying off, the immediate gaps we are fixing, and the one ask we have for every team."
[Point to Slide 1 - Wins] "First, the wins: Dedicated pilots are converting, Optimize recommendations reduced test token spend, and we avoided a larger outage thanks to routing fallbacks."
[Slide 2 - OKRs] "Here are the three company-level objectives we want every team to link to. After this meeting, please pick the single backlog item that best moves one of these KRs and add it to the tracker."
[Close] "We’ll take a few questions. If your topic needs deeper follow-up, we’ll capture it and come back within two weeks."

Notes to self
- Keep the live slide deck minimal; use the lightboard for pointing and emphasis.
- Ensure rehearsals include the triage moderator.
- Push for recording + searchable transcript and tag by OKR so we can later surface Q&A per objective.

-- end of facilitator pack (draft) --

Document history
- v0-1: initial skeleton (A. Chen, 2026-02-18)
- v0-2: added OKR KRs and early exec crib (R. Morgan, 2026-02-25)
- v0-3: rehearsal script and action owners updated (S. Desai, 2026-03-05)
